svg.aria-label: Gray's Anatomy engraving of the front of the right thigh and groin with the femoral artery and nerve marked. The inguinal ligament is highlighted between the anterior superior iliac spine and the pubic tubercle. The femoral artery is circled just below the ligament, the femoral vein is drawn as a dashed line just medial to it, and the puncture site is marked one to two centimeters below the ligament and just medial to the artery. Plate by Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy 1918, public domain.
svg.text: The femoral vein, from bone landmarks
Right thigh. For a left femoral line, mirror it.
The line between the two is
Bone landmarks, not the skin crease.
In obesity the crease can sit centimeters below the ligament, among
branching vessels. Above the ligament, a puncture bleeds into the
retroperitoneum. Lateral to medial: nerve, artery, vein.
Plate: H. V. Carter, Gray’s Anatomy, 20th ed. (1918), fig. 1245 — public domain
Vein and puncture site drawn by hand; the plate shows artery and nerve.
